title: About half of viewers miss a gorilla strolling through a video
body: In a famous 1999 study by Daniel Simons and Christopher Chabris, people watched a video of players passing basketballs and counted one team’s passes. Midway through, a person in a gorilla suit walked right through the scene, and in most groups about half the viewers never noticed. Attention works like a spotlight: when it is locked onto a demanding task, even striking but unexpected things can go completely unseen. It is called inattentional blindness.
